title: Beneath the Silence
subtitle: A newly emerging darkness covers the land.

items.text: Beneath the Silence
Riverside, Steppe

items.speaker: Sergey
items.text: Hey! I got something! Sasha, come give me a hand!
Not far from the camp, Sergey has been watering the horses while he fishes, undeterred by the danger brewing across the steppe.
The fishnet he failed to steal last year ended up in his pack before he left home. Old Somov put it there himself.

items.speaker: Zeno Cavalryman I
items.text: Got it! Dear Lord, this is heavy!

items.speaker: Sergey
items.text: Must be a big one. Come on, Sasha, put your back into it.
The two young men, children of this very river, use all their strength to drag the fishnet to the riverbank.

items.speaker: Zeno Cavalryman I
items.text: Have you ever caught a fish this big before?

items.speaker: Sergey
items.text: Never! The fish done all the growing this year instead of the crops?

items.speaker: Sergey
items.text: Just a bit further. Grab tight. On my mark. One! Two! Three!
They stumble back as they finally haul the net ashore.

items.speaker: Zeno Cavalryman I
items.text: Go check it out. I dare say even my grandpa has never seen fish so big.
Sergey runs to the net and untangles the cords like an expert.
*cough*
That's not a sound a fish would make.

items.speaker: Sergey
items.text: Huh? Thi-This is—
*cough*

items.speaker: Zeno Cavalryman I
items.text: What kind of fish is it, Sergey?
Sasha hurries over to join him.

items.speaker: Sergey
items.text: I'll be damned! Sasha! It's a person?

items.speaker: Zeno Cavalryman I
items.text: A person? Have you lost your mind?
*cough* Help. Help me.

items.speaker: Sergey
items.text: Damn it! Hurry up, will you? It's a living person! We have to take her to camp!

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: Hmm?
The sound of dozens of horses neighing at once echoes from somewhere far away.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: Andreas? Charon? Where *cough* where am I?
Warm, dry air sweeps across her cheeks. She hears the crackle of burning willow sticks.

items.speaker: Sergey
items.text: You're awake? Try getting to your feet.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: Ergh. My head's spinning. I can hardly ...

items.speaker: Sergey
items.text: Whoa, whoa, easy now. Just try and take a few steps. It'll help, trust me.
Merel doesn't know how she gets to her feet. All she remembers is swaying as she somehow pulled herself upright.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: I ... What is this place?

items.speaker: Sergey
items.text: Relax. You're in the Zeno Cavalry Corps camp. It's safe here.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: Z-Zeno? Oh, you've got to be kidding.
That name is like a hell-bent killer pursuing her to the ends of the earth.
Sergey doesn't notice the unusual panic that grips her. To him, she's simply a frightened lost girl.
Merel looks around and sees a soldier in a different uniform walking toward her.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Sergey, I heard you found a girl.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: No. It can't be ...

items.speaker: Sergey
items.text: We fished her out of the river, Lieutenant. She just woke up.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: And you just brought her straight into camp? She's obviously not a local. What if she's a rebel spy, huh?

items.speaker: Sergey
items.text: Sure, she's not a local, but she doesn't seem like a bandit either.
Lilya steps closer and stares at her for a long while.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Hm. Fair enough. What's your name?

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: I—
She falters before she can say the false name she created. Under Lieutenant Lilya's piercing gaze, the girl loses the courage to lie.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: M-Merel.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Merel? Not from around here, then. How'd you end up in the water?

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: I, uh, I came seeking refuge near the river, and then, I ... I was chased by some people—bandits or something.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: I tried to escape, but I fell off my horse and into the river.
Hearing her tale of misfortune, Lilya shakes her head helplessly and turns to Sergey.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Send her somewhere safe after she recovers. We'll decamp tomorrow morning, station in Tamarovka for a day, and then head to the city. Commander's orders.

items.speaker: Sergey
items.text: Really? That's my home! I can visit my aunt and uncle! I can sleep in my own bed for a night!

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: You'll have to apply for leave to do that. You eaten anything, Merel? We still got some canned meat from the Foundation.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: Canned meat ...
The temptation of canned meat outweighs all fear of the Foundation. She swallows her saliva.
After the lieutenant leaves, Sergey returns to his usual complaining.

items.speaker: Sergey
items.text: Too bad I only caught you today, huh?

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: Um, s-sorry?

items.speaker: Sergey
items.text: Don't worry. It's not every day you fish a person out of the river, hahaha. Oh, by the way, you can stay at my uncle's when we arrive in Tamarovka if you like.

items.speaker: Sergey
items.text: It's no Winter Palace, but it's better than a tent, that's for sure.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: You live with your uncle?

items.speaker: Sergey
items.text: Yeah. Father died at the front four years ago, and my mother was sick—lost her two years later. My aunt and uncle took me in.

items.speaker: Sergey
items.text: I do have to do farm work to earn my keep, but that's no big deal.

items.speaker: Sergey
items.text: How about you? Where are you from? You said you're a refugee. Where's your family now?
The girl stares at the empty ground before her.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: I don't have a family.
Even the ever-slippery Sergey loses his smile. He can't help but think of that winter when his mother lay dying.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: An, um, orphanage took me in. I grew up there.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: Are there many locals in the cavalry? Like you?

items.speaker: Sergey
items.text: Yeah, most of us actually. Back when Zeno first got here, there were only a thousand people. The Cavalry Corps didn't even exist.

items.speaker: Sergey
items.text: When the famine struck the steppe, and even potatoes wouldn't grow, the cavalry gave us food and shelter.

items.speaker: Sergey
items.text: So I thought, maybe it wouldn't be too bad to join them. At least then I could save some food for my family.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: But you've enlisted in an army. You'll have to fight.

items.speaker: Sergey
items.text: But I haven't had to yet. And everyone's alive and fitter than ever. Isn't that enough?

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Friends already, huh?
She precisely tosses a can of meat into Merel's arms.

items.speaker: Sergey
items.text: Nothing for me, Lieutenant?

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Too slow. Got to get it yourself now.
Merel, silent among their chatter, stares at the Foundation symbol on the can for a long while.
Finally, she slips her index finger under the ring and pulls the can open. She lowers her head and sips the oily gravy.
There was a time I thought you would lead us to the eternal. I thought you were like me—a man with ambition, a leader worth following.
But look what you've become. A coward.
You buckled while I stood tall. I have far excelled you, Igor, and the world will worship me for it.
He whips out his pistol, aims at the tall figure blocking his way, and pulls the trigger, only to hear the faint click of the firing pin.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: No mortal can transcend eternity, Krutov.
His opponent calmly draws his shashka.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: Your arrogance has gone beyond your means, turning you cruel and foolish. How disappointing.

items.speaker: Krutov
items.text: You can't kill me, Igor. You—
Shouts, gunfire, curses, as men shove past one another and hooves kick up an almost scalding dust.

items.speaker: Escort Soldier
items.text: Bring everyone here! Separate the arcanists from the humans! Zeno's captives in their own line! Move it, slackers!
He wakes from his restless dreams. Incense still lingers in the air around him, the hateful scent of henbane clinging to his nostrils.
Tent, Krutov's Encampment

items.speaker: Krutov
items.text: Useless. I knew that witless ritualist was not to be trusted.

items.speaker: Ritualist
items.text: General Krutov.
As if having foreseen that the man in the tent would awake, an oddly dressed ritualist slips inside.

items.speaker: Ritualist
items.text: You have awoken, yet the incense has yet to fade. I suggest you return to your dreams until you're capable of overcoming your nightmare.

items.speaker: Krutov
items.text: Enough of your riddles and trickery. Why are you here?

items.speaker: Ritualist
items.text: Captives. The first batch has arrived.

items.speaker: Krutov
items.text: Then you do as we agreed: Take the arcanists and leave the rest to me. What part of that do you not understand?

items.speaker: Ritualist
items.text: There is a peculiar individual among the captives—an Awakened. We didn't discuss how to deal with them.

items.speaker: Krutov
items.text: An Awakened. Those can be particularly useful. What do you know of it?

items.speaker: Ritualist
items.text: Thanks to the knowledge bestowed by Her, I was able to glean some insight. Though, I'm surprised to have encountered it here.

items.speaker: Ritualist
items.text: It seems the human fools named it after a mythological deity, as if by doing so, it would somehow render it capable of resting their sinful souls in peace.

items.speaker: Krutov
items.text: Interesting. Take me to it.
Tent, Krutov's Encampment
Between the thudding of sandbags hitting the ground, bursts of gunfire echo through the camp.
Having already given his life to the tragedy of this age, Charon has already sensed what is happening around him.
He wants to leave but cannot move. Not long ago, a ritualist scratched a series of symbols beneath his feet, binding him to the spot.

items.speaker: Krutov
items.text: Charon, is it?
He senses the approaching footsteps only when they are already close, then turns toward the voice.

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: Why did you kill those who surrendered?

items.speaker: Krutov
items.text: Well, too many mouths to feed. There isn't enough food across the entire Don to keep everyone alive through the winter.

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: You could have set them free. They were only civilians. They would cause you no trouble.

items.speaker: Krutov
items.text: Civilian implies civilization—civility, wouldn't you say? The Cossacks are barbarians. Setting them free would only bolster my enemies. I will not take the risk.
Charon lowers his head in silence. It seems there are no words left in him.

items.speaker: Krutov
items.text: Intriguing. Just as the ritualist said. Tell me, are you able to foresee a man's death?

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: The shadow of death lingers over these grasslands. Countless will die in a killing driven by starvation and hatred. That is what brought me here.
Krutov looks off to the edge of the camp, where the yellow pasture grass bows gently on small rises.
Gunfire crackles again, along with the sound of something crashing to the ground.

items.speaker: Krutov
items.text: A shadow, you say? I see a man walking the grasslands, the dead nourishing the soil. He stands amid a bountiful harvest. I am that man.

items.speaker: Krutov
items.text: Your "shadow of death" means nothing. What I need is a precise prophecy, one for a single man, for me.

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: I cannot do such a thing. Nor is there any desire to.

items.speaker: Krutov
items.text: I am offering you a chance, Awakened. Serve me and my army, and I will spare you the ritualist's hand.

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: Ritualist?
Krutov gestures toward the binding ritual beneath Charon with his chin.

items.speaker: Krutov
items.text: This is her work. She tells me you dispelled another incantation cast by her kind on a human soldier.

items.speaker: Krutov
items.text: She's desperate to tear you apart and see how you did it. Some special arcane skill, she claims.

items.speaker: Krutov
items.text: Trust me. What she will do to you is one thing you do not want to foresee.

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: Manus Vindictae.

items.speaker: Krutov
items.text: Ah, so you can see some specifics. Well? What is your decision?

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: No. Neither your enemy nor your ally. There is nothing I can do for you but bury the dead.
Krutov fixes a sharp gaze on Charon, as if he could tear through the cloth covering his face with sight alone.

items.speaker: Krutov
items.text: Difference of opinion, hmph?

items.speaker: Krutov
items.text: Why am I surprised? You're just like the rest of them. One bad decision after another!
His cursing seems to be directed at some invisible onlooker rather than at Charon.

items.speaker: Krutov
items.text: And I am left to right their wrongs. It seems only I can.

items.speaker: Krutov
items.text: I gave you your chance, freak.
